transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Asteria Head of Security), Daniel Cho (Asteria Platform), Ruth Alvarez (Asteria Compliance)

Auto-summary: quick run-through of certs, SSO/SCIM, KMS and prompt retention options. Action items noted.

00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Marco from our infra and security team is with me.
00:12 Marco Ruiz: hi all, Marco here. i'll try to focus on the technical controls and answer the integration questions.
00:20 Priya Menon: thanks, lena. quick agenda ask: we really need confirmation on two things up front — SOC 2 and the statement about customer prompts not being used to train models. also KMS and retention.
00:34 Lena Park: sure, we'll hit those. quick intro — asteria's use case, are you planning to send PHI into the model or is it mostly metadata?
00:46 Daniel Cho: there will be patient-identifiable data in a subset of flows, so PHI is in scope. we need HIPAA-level controls and a clear stance on training.
00:58 Ruth Alvarez: and we have strict EU residency requirements for some data sets, need to understand region pinning.
01:10 Marco Ruiz: understood. starting with compliance posture: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II in the hosted product, we also have ISO 27001 summary. i'll send the PDFs after the call. note: our SOC2 covers the inference platform and operational controls for dedicated instances as well, see the pdf.
01:32 Priya Menon: is that SOC2 for the hosted service only or does it cover Dedicated & Private as well? sometimes vendor reports exclude dedicated clusters.
01:44 Marco Ruiz: good question — the report covers our control environment and processes; for Dedicated/Private deployments we operate under similar controls but we provide additional attestations and deployment-specific hardening. we'll include language in the DPA.
01:58 Daniel Cho: can you confirm whether Redwood ever uses customer prompt/content to further train open models? we need an explicit no-training confirmation.
02:10 Lena Park: yes — important: Redwood does not use customer content to train models by default. for hosted we have an opt-in ML research program which is explicitly gated and requires customer opt-in and contractual agreement. enterprise contracts typically prohibit training on customer data unless agreed. we'll provide the exact wording.
02:34 Priya Menon: can you put that in writing in the DPA and the security pack?
02:40 Lena Park: yes, we'll include a clause: "Customer content is not used to train models without explicit written consent".
02:48 Marco Ruiz: switching to auth: SSO and identity — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with customizable roles, and API keys can be scoped.
03:07 Ruth Alvarez: do you support SCIM group sync for provisioning and automatic deprovisioning?
03:15 Marco Ruiz: yes, SCIM group sync is supported; we can disable interactive SSO for dedicated instances and enforce SAML only.
03:25 Daniel Cho: how do you handle audit logs? retention, fields, and export? we need 12 month retention and exports to our SIEM (Splunk).
03:35 Marco Ruiz: we export audit logs in JSON lines; fields include user_id, api_key_id, action_type, request_path, timestamps, request and response hashes — sensitive payloads are redacted by default. retention on the platform is 90 days for hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure longer retention or ship logs to customer infra.
03:57 Priya Menon: so for hosted we get 90 days but we can push streaming logs to our S3 or Splunk for 12 months?
04:04 Marco Ruiz: correct, we provide log forwarding and SIEM connectors; streaming export is supported for enterprise customers.
04:12 Ruth Alvarez: about redaction — what exactly is redacted in logs? PHI often ends up in prompts.
04:20 Marco Ruiz: we redact full prompt bodies in audit logs by default for hosted. you can choose to keep hashed prompt references and metadata like token counts. for Dedicated we can configure field-level redaction or tokenization.
04:38 Daniel Cho: KMS — do you support BYOK and HSM integration? key rotation policies?
04:44 Marco Ruiz: yes. BYOK via customer-managed keys in major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). we support envelope encryption, and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. rotation is supported; you control rotation schedule, and we support key rotation without re-encrypting all stored artifacts via envelope keys. i'll send the KMS integration guide.
05:10 Priya Menon: region residency — we need to guarantee EU-only storage for certain datasets. can you pin storage and inference to eu-west-1?
05:19 Marco Ruiz: yes, we have region pinning and routing policies. for data-in-transit we use TLS 1.2+ and can guarantee processing region for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can request region tenancy.
05:33 Ruth Alvarez: what's your data retention policy for prompts and model context? how long are prompts stored?
05:40 Marco Ruiz: default: ephemeral cache for KV/prefix caching during session, short-lived (minutes). we store prompts in a retention store for up to 30 days for analytics and safety by default on hosted. however enterprise customers can opt to disable retention entirely or set custom retention windows; Dedicated has configurable retention.
06:02 Priya Menon: do you support on-write purge APIs for customer data? we need a programmatic purge endpoint for DSR (data subject requests).
06:12 Marco Ruiz: yes, we expose a delete/purge API that can remove stored prompts, traces, and cached context. we'll include steps and caveats — e.g. some cold backups may persist within backup windows; we document RTO for full purge.
06:28 Daniel Cho: what's your approach to PII/PHI detection and redaction? automatic or customer-driven?
06:34 Marco Ruiz: we provide optional PII detection pipelines that can be enabled; they flag and optionally redact fields prior to logging or storage. for high-sensitivity flow we recommend application-side redaction prior to sending.
06:48 Priya Menon: HIPAA — do you sign a BAA? how does Redwood handle PHI in hosted vs private?
06:56 Lena Park: we do offer BAAs for customers with HIPAA needs. For hosted we require a BAA and Dedicated or Private deployments are recommended for high-volume PHI. we'll include standard HIPAA controls in the package.
07:12 Ruth Alvarez: penetration testing and vuln disclosures — do you run external pentests and publish an attestation?
07:19 Marco Ruiz: we run annual external pentests and have a third-party vuln management program. we can share a summary of findings redacted for sensitivity and provide a point of contact for coordinated disclosure.
07:32 Priya Menon: legal question — subprocessors list and data transfer mechanisms to third parties (e.g., vector DB providers).
07:40 Lena Park: we maintain a subprocessors list; typical partners include cloud providers and observability vendors. we'll share the current list with the DPA. Transfers to third parties are covered in the DPA with standard SCCs for EU transfers.
07:55 Daniel Cho: technical deep-dive request: can we see a demo of audit log streaming and KMS integration? also a private tenant trial to try retention settings?
08:06 Lena Park: yes, we'll set up a dedicated trial env. Marco will run the deep-dive.
08:12 Marco Ruiz: noted. i'll schedule a 90-minute tech session and demo the KMS flow (BYOK) and log streaming.
08:20 Priya Menon: one more — encryption at rest details, algorithm, and whether customer keys are used to encrypt model cache and stored artifacts.
08:30 Marco Ruiz: we use AES-256 for at-rest encryption. with BYOK we wrap data keys with customer keys. model KV caches in memory aren't persisted unless configured; any persisted caches are envelope-encrypted.
08:44 Daniel Cho: question about service segregation — can we get a VPC-only deployment? we want no public internet egress for inference traffic.
08:52 Marco Ruiz: Private deployment supports VPC-only and optionally air-gapped on-prem. Dedicated can be configured with private networking and egress restrictions.
09:04 Priya Menon: are there SOC2 controls around change management and code deployment that we can map to our internal controls?
09:12 Marco Ruiz: yes, our SOC2 covers change management, access approvals, and CI/CD checks; we'll provide the control mapping spreadsheet.
09:22 Ruth Alvarez: how do you handle employee access to customer data? is there privileged access logging and justification?
09:30 Marco Ruiz: privileged access is tightly controlled, RBAC + Just-In-Time access with approval flows. all privileged actions are logged and require two-person approval for production infra.
09:44 Daniel Cho: do you have an SLA for data deletion when requested? what's the timeline for complete deletion across backups?
09:52 Marco Ruiz: typical deletion from hot storage is immediate; backups have a documented retention and purge window — full removal across cold backups can take up to 90 days depending on backup cycles, we'll document exact RTOs per deployment model.
10:08 Priya Menon: Mia question — sorry, i mean, Marco, can you also clarify model telemetry collection? some providers collect usage data for quality analysis.
10:18 Marco Ruiz: we collect anonymized telemetry by default; request-level data is hashed and aggregated for QoS. telemetry is optional and can be disabled for enterprise customers.
10:30 Ruth Alvarez: do you have a documented incident response plan and SLA for breach notification?
10:38 Marco Ruiz: yes, we have an IR plan with 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents and a dedicated incident commander. larger customers can negotiate faster timelines in contracts.
10:50 Priya Menon: ok, so lets talk about a concrete retention setup: we want prompts stored 0 days in hosted (i.e., no retention), but log streaming to our S3 for 18 months. feasible?
11:02 Marco Ruiz: hosted default doesn't do 0 by default, but enterprise can disable retention; we can route logs to your S3 for 18 months. for the no-retention path we'd recommend Dedicated/Private for stronger guarantees.
11:18 Daniel Cho: how are exports authenticated? do you push to a signed S3 role or do we pull?
11:25 Marco Ruiz: we support push via cross-account S3 role (recommended) or you can pull from a secure endpoint. we'll include both options in the integration doc.
11:38 Priya Menon: about the training question again — if we opt into any support program or benchmark program, does that expose prompts to research?
11:46 Lena Park: yes, opt-in programs are explicit and contractual; they require data to be isolated and consented. default is no research usage.
11:55 Daniel Cho: any rate-limits or masking for high-frequency PII flows?
12:02 Marco Ruiz: we have throttle controls and burst protections; masking should be implemented at app layer for best practice. we can also set policy-based input filters.
12:15 (several minutes of clarifying back-and-forth and short interruptions omitted for brevity)
26:00 Marco Ruiz: demo notes: i'll show how a BYOK key is attached — you upload a public key, we wrap data keys, we rotate on schedule. note that HSM-backed keys require extra provisioning steps on the cloud provider side.
26:35 Priya Menon: can we redact PHI at the field level prior to storage? automatic redaction is helpful but not perfect.
26:45 Marco Ruiz: yes, field-level redaction policies are supported and can be run before storage; again app-side redaction is recommended for deterministic results.
27:10 Ruth Alvarez: regulatory: for EU data subjects, DSRs — you can accept a subject request via API or will we need to route through support?
27:20 Marco Ruiz: we provide APIs for DSR-driven purge requests; support is available for manual assistance for edge cases.
27:34 Priya Menon: what about encryption for logs in transit to our SIEM?
27:40 Marco Ruiz: we push logs over TLS and support signed delivery to S3. logs can also be encrypted at rest with your S3 keys.
27:52 Daniel Cho: anything about model drift telemetry or quality monitoring that exposes prompts?
28:01 Marco Ruiz: quality monitoring uses hashed references and sample-sampling on explicit consent; we won't sample raw prompts unless allowed.
28:18 Priya Menon: ok that's good. question on contract terms — liability caps and indemnification for PHI breaches? we need to cover that in legal.
28:28 Lena Park: legal will work with your team; we've done BAAs and PHI clauses before. we can pull in our legal ops to confirm language.
28:40 Ruth Alvarez: open question: can we get a red-team report or recent pentest executive summary?
28:48 Marco Ruiz: yes, we'll provide a redacted pentest exec summary.
29:00 (customer pauses)
29:12 Daniel Cho: operational question — how are model updates handled? do you control rollout windows and can we pin model versions?
29:22 Marco Ruiz: you can pin to model versions and control rollouts. automatic fallbacks exist if a model backend is degraded. model updates are controlled via release channels and you can choose to opt-out of automatic model upgrades.
29:40 Priya Menon: any certifications for supply chain security?
29:48 Marco Ruiz: we have vendor risk assessments and follow NIST guidelines; we'll share our supplier assessment template.
30:05 Lena Park: ok we're getting close on time. quick recap and next steps?
30:12 Priya Menon: yes please recap.
30:15 Lena Park: recap: Redwood confirmed SOC2 and ISO posture, will share artifacts; explicit no-training on customer data unless opt-in and contractual; KMS BYOK options supported; we can stream logs to customer's SIEM and configure retention windows; Dedicated/Private recommended for strict EU-residency and zero-retention guarantees; BAA available for HIPAA; SCIM/SAML and RBAC supported; purge API and DSR flow available.
30:44 Ruth Alvarez: that's right. next steps: receive docs and schedule tech deep-dive.
30:50 Lena Park: action items as discussed — i'll send the pack.
30:55 Marco Ruiz: i'll follow up with KMS guide and schedule the 90-min deep dive.
31:02 Priya Menon: thanks — we'll share internal list of required audit fields and retention SLAs.
31:08 Lena Park: perfect. any final quick q's?
31:12 Daniel Cho: one small thing, can you confirm the default log redaction removes raw prompt bodies from non-configured logs?
31:20 Marco Ruiz: yes, default hosted audit logs redact raw prompt bodies; we'll state that in the security pack.
31:28 Priya Menon: thanks everyone.
31:32 (call wraps up, small cross-talk)
31:45 Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with artifacts and the next tech session invite.
31:52 Meeting end.
